text:
incident-bot: ALERT: P99 latency spike on /v1/generate (service: inference-gateway) - Sev 2. Paging oncall. Incident ID: INC-1994. Autoscaling didn't keep up.
Alex Kim: I'm on it — I'm primary for this shift, taking driver.
Maya Ortega: I'll own comms and customer updates. tagging CSMs once we have impact. :thumbsup:
Priya Singh: Quick ask — which customers are seeing errors vs just latency?
Alex Kim: Initial look: 5% elevated 5xx across the US region, most traffic hitting model-a-small on dedicated pool. No full outages reported from customers yet, but p99 up from ~180ms -> 2.1s.
Sam Lee: FYI I have a 40m gap starting in ~7m (end of overlap). If this stays open I'll need someone as secondary.
Jordan Park: I'm wrapping a deploy in 3m, won't be able to take pager.
Alex Kim: Noted. Maya — can you be secondary for the next 40m? If you're tied to comms we'll need another for troubleshooting.
Maya Ortega: I can be comms and secondary for now, but I'll escalate if we need hands-on infra.
Priya Singh: If we end up routing to fallback model we should inform Prod Eng + Billing (potential cost impact).
Alex Kim: Plan proposal: 1) short-term mitigate by draining long-tail batches and fall back route to model-a-quant for non-critical customers, 2) scale up dedicated pool if autoscaler doesn't react, 3) collect traces for root cause (likely batching config).
Maya Ortega: I'll draft a short customer note once we confirm fallback route.
Alex Kim: Running checks now:
```
# check inference pods and queues
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=model-a
kubectl -n inference exec -it svc/queue-metrics -- curl /metrics | grep queue_length
```
Alex Kim: Seeing queue_length spikes on node inference-gpu-3 and model-a-deployment has repeated preemption logs.
Priya Singh: Any recent rollout on model-a or gateway?
Jordan Park: There was a small gateway config push 14m ago that toggled batching_v2 = true for /v1/generate. I'm rolling that back to test.
Alex Kim: Good catch. If batching_v2 is more aggressive it might be creating the long-tail. Jordan, proceed with rollback when you can.
Jordan Park: Rolling back now.
incident-bot: Deploy rollback in progress for gateway config (deploy-789).
Alex Kim: While that happens I'll start a controlled traffic split: 15% -> model-a-quant fallback. Command:
```
# traffic split (internal tool)
redwoodctl traffic-split set --route /v1/generate --weights model-a:85,model-a-quant:15 --reason "mitigate p99 latency"
```
Maya Ortega: Executed the traffic-split command. Monitoring customer error rates.
Priya Singh: Can you post the runbook link for this incident?
Alex Kim: Runbook: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/inference/p99-latency. Key sections: "traffic split", "drain healthy nodes", "scale dedicated pool".
Sam Lee: After rollback + traffic-split, queues look lower on node-3. p99 dropping to ~600ms (still elevated).
Maya Ortega: Draft for customers: "We're investigating increased latencies on inference endpoints; traffic is being routed to fallback variants to reduce impact. We'll update in 30m or on further changes." Want me to send?
Priya Singh: Yes please, include that we're monitoring and no data loss. Tag CSMs: @csm-elaine @csm-ryan.
Maya Ortega: Posted note to #customers with CSM tags.
Alex Kim: Next steps: if p99 > 1.5s after 10m, scale dedicated pool + cordon problematic host.
Jordan Park: Rollback complete. Gateway config back to batching_v1.
incident-bot: ALERT: deploy-789 rollback succeeded.
Sam Lee: After rollback and split, error rates back to baseline, p99 ~220ms. Looks stable.
Maya Ortega: I'll keep comms cadence every 20m until incident resolved.
Alex Kim: Assigning ownership: driver = Alex Kim, comms = Maya Ortega, secondary (coverage) = Priya Singh for next 40m.
Priya Singh: Acknowledged.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-1994 status -> monitoring. Assigned: Alex Kim (driver), Maya Ortega (comms).
Maya Ortega: Sending final customer update once we hit 30m stable.
Alex Kim: Adding a follow-up action: open a postmortem ticket and add to next runbook review — probable cause: batching_v2 tuning mismatch.
Priya Singh: I'll create the postmortem draft and add action items 1) add automated canary for batching toggle, 2) adjust autoscaler thresholds.
Sam Lee: Good handoff. I'm stepping off now — Alex take over in case anything flares.
Alex Kim: Thanks Sam. I'll keep monitoring for the next 30m then update runbook.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: INC-1994 -> mitigated. Duration: 00:23:14.
Maya Ortega: Final note posted to #incidents and #customers. Closing handoff: driver Alex Kim, comms Maya Ortega. :white_check_mark:
